history.heading: Ancient Libya
paragraphs: Libya's coast was home to Amazigh (Berber) peoples and later to Phoenician and Greek colonies. Greek Cyrene in the east and the Phoenician cities of Tripolitania in the west, such as Leptis Magna and Sabratha, flourished under Roman rule; their ruins are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Rock art in the Acacus Mountains records life in the Sahara thousands of years ago.

history.heading: Arab and Ottoman rule
paragraphs: Arab armies brought Islam in the 7th century. Tripoli later became an Ottoman province, ruled for long periods by the semi-independent Karamanli dynasty, whose corsairs fought the United States in the Barbary Wars of the early 19th century. In the east, the Senussi religious order became influential.

history.heading: Italian colony and monarchy
paragraphs: Italy invaded in 1911 and faced fierce resistance, led by Omar Mukhtar until his execution in 1931; Italian repression killed many thousands. After the Second World War, Libya became independent on 24 December 1951 as a kingdom under King Idris. Oil was discovered in 1959.

history.heading: Gaddafi and after
paragraphs: In 1969 Colonel Muammar Gaddafi seized power in a coup. He ruled for 42 years with an idiosyncratic ideology described in his Green Book, nationalising oil and supporting militant groups abroad, which led to international sanctions after the 1988 Lockerbie bombing.

In 2011 an uprising, supported by NATO air strikes, overthrew Gaddafi, who was killed. Libya then fragmented among rival militias and governments. A civil war from 2014 pitted the western-based government in Tripoli against eastern forces led by Khalifa Haftar. A 2020 ceasefire has largely held, but the country remains divided.

culture.heading: Society
paragraphs: Arabic is the official language, and Amazigh languages are spoken by minorities, along with Tuareg and Tebu communities in the south. Nearly all Libyans are Sunni Muslim. Tribal and family ties are important in society and politics.
Libyan cuisine includes couscous, bazeen (a barley dough dish), shorba (soup) and dates. Ghadames, an oasis town, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

politics.heading: Divided country
paragraphs: Libya has rival authorities: an internationally recognised Government of National Unity in Tripoli and a rival government in the east backed by Haftar's Libyan National Army. UN-led efforts to hold national elections have repeatedly stalled.
Foreign powers, including Türkiye, Russia, Egypt and the UAE, have backed different sides. Libya is a major transit country for migrants seeking to reach Europe, many of whom face abuse.

economy.heading: Oil economy
paragraphs: Libya has Africa's largest proven oil reserves, and oil and gas provide almost all exports and government revenue. Production has often been disrupted by conflict and blockades. Much of the population is employed by the state.

Rival control over the central bank and oil revenues is a key source of conflict. The currency is the Libyan dinar. In 2023 floods caused by Storm Daniel destroyed much of the city of Derna, killing thousands.
